title: Sternum displacement relative to the thoracic vertebra during breathing

quantity.name: sternum displacement
quantity.definition: change of the sternal-body origin position expressed in the thoracic vertebra frame (x anterior, y cephalic, z lateral) between lung-volume poses

source.authors: Beyer B, Feipel V, Sholukha V, Cheze L, Van Sint Jan S
source.sample: 12 asymptomatic adults, retrospective spiral CT at TLC, MIC, FRC (same sample as Beyer 2014/2015 CVJ studies per the authors)

protocol.summary: CT-based sternum and vertebra frames; displacement of sternum position vector in vertebral frame.
how_to_use: Prescribe or check sternum excursion from FRC to TLC of ~18 mm cephalic and ~10 mm anterior relative to the thoracic spine (supine); lateral ~0.
Note that below MIC the sternum moves both anteriorly and cephalically, above MIC mainly cephalically (Fig 2).
Link rib rotation to sternal cephalic displacement d (mm) with the regressions (Fig 9) to scale a breathing model to a target sternum excursion.

measurement.device: Siemens SOMATOM spiral CT, 0.5 mm slices, 1 mm spacing; virtual palpation of 5 landmarks per bone (lhpFusionBox)
measurement.posture: supine, breath-hold against closed airway (spirometer-controlled), upper limbs raised above head
measurement.task: static breath-holds at TLC, MIC and FRC

equations: CVJ1 ROM (deg) = 0.8109*d + 1.933, R2=0.897, p<0.001 (d = sternum cephalo-caudal displacement, mm; Fig 9A)
SCJ1 ROM (deg) = 0.6348*d + 3.3277, R2=0.8419, p<0.01 (Fig 9B; label placement in figure is swapped, assignment from line slopes and text r=0.92)
protocol.notes: Text says displacement 'relative to vertebra Th1' while Methods and Fig 2 use the Th7 frame. Text +- values treated as SD (Fig 2 bars are SE and smaller); digitised SE of x (1.71) and y (2.13) imply SDs ~5.9 and ~7.4, i.e. the text SDs for x (7.1) and y (5.9) may be swapped. Abstract: cephalic displacement 17.8-19.2 mm over IC.

extraction.uncertainty: text exact; Fig 2 digitised +-0.3 mm (22 px/mm at 300 dpi)
extraction.check_notes: Fig 2 FRC-TLC digitised (9.6, 17.8, 0.8 mm) matches text values; regression equations copied from figure text, assignment of SCJ1/SCJ7 checked against plotted line slopes (SCJ1 line rises ~19 deg over 29 mm) and text r values (0.92, 0.74).

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
